evidence.quote: We construct such a condition for every smooth quintic threefold.

outputs.exact_statement:
Every smooth complex quintic threefold admits a numerical Bridgeland stability condition $\sigma=(Z,\mathcal P)$ with the support property on $K_{\mathrm{num}}(X)_{\mathbb R}$ such that, for every $E\in\mathcal D$ and $\varphi\in\mathbb R$, $$Z(\Phi E)=e^{2\pi i/5}Z(E),\qquad
 \Phi\bigl(\mathcal P(\varphi)\bigr)=\mathcal P(\varphi+2/5),\qquad
 Z(\mathcal O_x)=-1$$ for every closed point $x\in X$.

Let $\Phi=T_{\mathcal O_X}\circ(-\otimes\mathcal O_X(1))$. There is a natural isomorphism of exact functors $$\label{eq:periodicity}
 \Phi^5\simeq[2].$$ Consequently $\Phi$ is an autoequivalence, with inverse $\Phi^4[-2]$.
The abelian categories $\mathcal B_{-1/2}$ and $\mathcal B_{1/2}$ are noetherian.

For every $b=\pm1/2$ and $\eta\in B_\delta$, the pair $(\mathcal T_b^\eta,\mathcal F_b^\eta)$ is a torsion pair. Its tilt has bounded heart and aisle $$\mathcal A_b^\eta=\langle\mathcal F_b^\eta[1],\mathcal T_b^\eta\rangle,
 \qquad \mathcal U_b^\eta
   =\{E\in W_b:H^0_{\mathcal B_b}(E)\in\mathcal T_b^\eta\}.$$ On $\mathcal A_b^\eta$ one has $N_b^\eta\geq0$, and no nonzero object of this heart has zero numerical class.

For all $\alpha,\theta\in B_\delta$, $$\mathcal O_X\in\mathcal A_-^\theta,\qquad
 \mathcal O_X[2]\in\mathcal A_+^\alpha,\qquad
 T_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal U_+^\alpha)\subset\mathcal U_-^\theta.$$

The blocks are extension closed, and $\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}(\mathcal S_j,\mathcal S_k)=0$ whenever $j>k$. Every object has a finite triangle filtration with nonzero factors in blocks of strictly decreasing indices. In $\mathcal H_k$ there is a torsion pair $$\label{eq:block-torsion-pair}
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal T_k=V_{k+1}\cap\mathcal H_k
     &=\langle\mathcal S_{k+4},\mathcal S_{k+3},
                \mathcal S_{k+2},\mathcal S_{k+1}\rangle,\\
 \mathcal F_k&=\mathcal S_k.
 \end{aligned}$$ In particular, $\mathcal S_k$ is closed under subobjects in $\mathcal H_k$.

Every nonzero object of $\mathcal S_k$ has a finite filtration by short exact sequences in $\mathcal H_k$, with all intermediate quotients in $\mathcal S_k$, whose nonzero factors are block-semistable with strictly decreasing phases.

If $E\in\mathcal S_k$ is block-semistable, then every nonzero subobject $G\subset E$ in $\mathcal H_k$ satisfies $\varphi_k(G)\le\varphi_k(E)$, without a saturation assumption. Consequently, for block-semistable $E,F\in\mathcal S_k$, $$\varphi_k(E)>\varphi_k(F)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}(E,F)=0.$$

For every real $c$, both pairs $$\label{eq:phase-cuts}
 \bigl(\mathcal P((c,\infty)),\mathcal P((-\infty,c])\bigr),
 \qquad
 \bigl(\mathcal P([c,\infty)),\mathcal P((-\infty,c))\bigr)$$ are an aisle and its right orthogonal for a bounded t-structure. Their hearts are respectively $\mathcal P((c,c+1])$ and $\mathcal P([c,c+1))$. Every interval category is the intersection of its lower and upper cut categories, with the indicated endpoint conventions. In particular, these categories, including each $\mathcal P(\varphi)$, are closed under direct summands.

For every interval $I$ of width less than one, with any choices of open or closed endpoints, $\mathcal P(I)$ is quasi-abelian. Its strict exact sequences are exactly the short exact sequences of a suitable bounded heart whose three terms belong to $\mathcal P(I)$.
Every phase interval of width less than one generates a finite-length quasi-abelian category. Hence the slicing in Proposition 16 is locally finite.
